newsitem.title: OMAN: New Omani law restricts foreign law firms' work.
newsitem.headline: New Omani law restricts foreign law firms' work.

text.p: Oman on Sunday issued a law restricting the work of foreign lawyers, saying they could set up partnerships with local law firms but would not be allowed to appear in court in seven years' time.

The law reorganising legal pratices in Oman was decreed by Oman's Sultan Qaboos bin Saeed and published in the official gazette. It said Omani law firms could still employ foreign lawyers, but prohibits practicing Omani lawyers from holding official posts or working outside the legal profession.
Arab lawyers can seek special permission to appear at Omani courts after the seven-year period, the law said.

Oman, like other Gulf Arab states where expatriates are an important part of the workforce, recently launched a drive to find more jobs for its nationals as part of efforts to diversify the economy and lessen dependence on oil-income
